name: Battle Ready Armor
tagline: Govern security work. Retain the knowledge.
summary: BRA runs directly on the host without requiring a separate VM or container. Registered SDK hooks connect managed tool requests to Body policy and engagement state. Supported model routing, tools, methods, browser/API access, terminal commands, and bounded assistant integrations share retained assessment records. Capture, finding acceptance, and reviewed promotion keep evidence and useful knowledge outside the model conversation.

features.title: Scope-first engagement
features.description: Define targets, exclusions, activity limits, and report requirements before work starts.
features.mechanism: The wizard records scope and tokens. Body Bash scope checks inspect one recognized target in the original command.

features.title: Method-driven work
features.description: Use target-specific phases, techniques, and deliverables.
features.mechanism: Target mapping and phase extraction create the engagement context.

features.title: Explicit authority
features.description: Inspect permissions outside the conversation.
features.mechanism: Named token readers inspect their supported environment, file, or ROE sources. Invocation approvals use separate identity and retry matching.

features.title: Block, decide, continue
features.description: Turn a denied request into a specific operator choice.
features.mechanism: Typed blocks retain tool input and connect grants to matching retries.

features.title: Control in Depth
features.description: Apply multiple controls around consequential requests.
features.mechanism: SDK adapters connect stop, approval, finding, command, and file checks.

features.title: Owned runtime paths
features.description: Keep artifacts, approvals, queues, and records in their designated locations.
features.mechanism: File policy and the runtime schema define permitted paths and writers.

features.title: Privacy aliases
features.description: Keep the same target relationship across context and execution.
features.mechanism: A local map connects word aliases with original values.

features.title: New-value review
features.description: Review newly detected chat values before the message continues.
features.mechanism: ANON-SCAN creates pending mapping decisions for the operator.

features.title: Local execution substitution
features.description: Resolve mapped alias commands locally and retain masked output.
features.mechanism: Original-command checks precede substitution. The guard executes locally and blocks duplicate SDK execution; no second target check evaluates the substituted command.

features.title: Evidence capture
features.description: Retain the tool output that supports later records.
features.mechanism: Capture identifiers, artifact paths, timestamps, and SHA-256 values enter the evidence index.

features.title: Origin-aware provenance
features.description: Connect a finding to the collection request that supports it.
features.mechanism: Capture resolution ranks original evidence above derivative inspection results.

features.title: Living assessment records
features.description: Keep intelligence, investigation leads, and findings distinct.
features.mechanism: Structured markers enter an event ledger and replay into their record streams.

features.title: Finding documentation
features.description: Create full issue records through a defined completion path.
features.mechanism: Queue scaffolds and deterministic evidence sections combine with restricted narrative tasks.

features.title: Finding recovery
features.description: Continue documentation after interruption or worker stalls.
features.mechanism: Queue reconciliation merges leftover outputs and supports a restricted main-agent handoff.

features.title: Reports and disclosure
features.description: Prepare executive, technical, vendor, and CNA outputs from engagement records.
features.mechanism: Close-out coordinates metadata, selection, generation, enhancement, and lessons.

features.title: Reviewed knowledge growth
features.description: Retain useful lessons in reusable methods, tools, skills, and patterns.
features.mechanism: Incremental and retrospective proposals enter operator review before promotion.

features.title: Separate exception recommendations
features.description: Keep reusable advice distinct from active engagement permission.
features.mechanism: Override promotion writes recommendations instead of enabling live bypasses.

features.title: Local model routing
features.description: Use a configured OpenAI-compatible inference backend.
features.mechanism: The optional completion clamp and LiteLLM sidecar preserve the SDK hook path.

features.title: Usage visibility
features.description: Inspect query usage and engagement progress.
features.mechanism: SDK result records supply token and cost summaries; telemetry reads engagement records.

features.title: Bounded external assistance
features.description: Expose selected status and action functions to an optional assistant.
features.mechanism: Separate service authentication, named resources, and expiring takeover leases govern the interface.

features.title: Voice integration
features.description: Route supported call actions through the configured provider.
features.mechanism: OpenClaw gateway calls or an installed Hermes plugin connect to the voice runtime.

features.title: Managed lifecycle
features.description: Resume, stop, package, back up, restore, or reset through explicit controls.
features.mechanism: Managed tasks, SDK process cleanup, durable records, and lifecycle scripts retain the engagement context.

flows.title: Scope to governed work
flows.summary: Turn an assessment request into a method-driven agent session with explicit scope and permission state.

steps.title: Receive scope
steps.detail: The engagement router passes scope and wizard actions to the managed lifecycle.

steps.title: Review privacy
steps.detail: Detection and the selected scope mode determine the operator mapping review.

steps.title: Write scope
steps.detail: The scope writer records targets, exclusions, authorization, and activity settings.

steps.title: Record tokens
steps.detail: Selected capabilities and modes become engagement approval state.

steps.title: Check readiness
steps.detail: Readiness routines inspect the structure, scripts, tools, and scope.

steps.title: Select the method
steps.detail: Target mapping chooses the supported method family and its phases.

steps.title: Build context
steps.detail: Phase context and host context supply the operational instructions.

steps.title: Prepare model routing
steps.detail: The manager prepares the SDK connection and optional local proxy.

steps.title: Register controls
steps.detail: The SDK wrapper installs the policy hooks and engagement-local state paths.

steps.title: Run and observe
steps.detail: The runner processes the turn while managed events update the operator interface.

flows.title: Alias command to documented finding
flows.summary: Trace original-command checks, local alias substitution, masked capture, and finding record acceptance.

steps.title: Use the known alias
steps.detail: The agent treats a mapped scope value as a usable target for the full engagement.

steps.title: Evaluate the tool request
steps.detail: Approval matching determines whether the proposed invocation can continue.

steps.title: Check command policy
steps.detail: Recognized activity, target, operation, path, and scan predicates inspect the original command. A word-only alias can produce no extracted target.

steps.title: Resolve local values
steps.detail: The local guard substitutes known aliases after original-command checks. It does not repeat target validation after substitution.

steps.title: Capture masked output
steps.detail: The intercept saves masked output and capture context, then blocks duplicate SDK execution.

steps.title: Index the evidence
steps.detail: The capture index retains identifiers, artifact paths, time, and hash information.

steps.title: Resolve the observation
steps.detail: The runner selects supporting provenance, preferring originating evidence.

steps.title: Write the marker event
steps.detail: Normalized marker fields enter the replayable event ledger.

steps.title: Create the finding scaffold
steps.detail: The enforcer adds the finding to its queue and creates its record structure.

steps.title: Derive evidence sections
steps.detail: System routines supply artifact references, hashes, reproduction details, and proof support files.

steps.title: Complete analysis
steps.detail: A restricted documentation task supplies the remaining narrative fields.

steps.title: Validate and review
steps.detail: The enforcer checks record requirements and applicable evidence references for operator inspection.

flows.title: Finding to retained doctrine
flows.summary: Prepare deliverables, derive useful lessons, and promote accepted values through a separate review boundary.

steps.title: Collect close-out metadata
steps.detail: End-intake supplies the fields required for the selected report types.

steps.title: Select findings
steps.detail: The optional selection step records which finding identifiers enter the report set.

steps.title: Generate report structure
steps.detail: Statistics and report routines read the structured engagement records.

steps.title: Prepare disclosure outputs
steps.detail: Vendor, CNA, and disclosure forms receive the selected content.

steps.title: Enhance and inspect
steps.detail: Narrative enhancement and placeholder checks expose retry or skip choices.

steps.title: Record lessons
steps.detail: Lessons routines combine findings, leads, review gaps, and assessment context.

steps.title: Derive candidates
steps.detail: Growth and incremental improvement write compact proposals from the recorded work.

steps.title: Review the pitch
steps.detail: The operator marks candidates as approved, denied, or deferred.

steps.title: Open promotion scope
steps.detail: A temporary template-write token surrounds supported promotion work.

steps.title: Route the accepted value
steps.detail: Promotion updates skills, tool knowledge, method drafts, attack patterns, or override recommendations.

steps.title: Record the result
steps.detail: Processed items receive implementation status and the temporary token is removed.

steps.title: Reuse with fresh authority
steps.detail: A later engagement consults the retained knowledge with its own scope, permissions, and evidence.

flows.title: Leased external assistance
flows.summary: Connect an optional assistant to bounded engagement resources and existing action routing.

steps.title: Authenticate the service
steps.detail: The external client supplies the separate 2x4 service token.

steps.title: Read a bounded summary
steps.detail: The API supplies the permitted engagement snapshot.

steps.title: Select a named resource
steps.detail: File and log routes accept allowed identifiers rather than unrestricted paths.

steps.title: Request takeover
steps.detail: The controller opens a limited confirmation period.

steps.title: Confirm the request
steps.detail: A valid confirmation creates the current control lease.

steps.title: Present the lease
steps.detail: Action requests supply the active lease identifier.

steps.title: Parse the action
steps.detail: The controller accepts supported structured actions and denies scope mutation approvals.

steps.title: Use engagement routing
steps.detail: Accepted actions enter the existing message router.

steps.title: Delegate call control
steps.detail: Supported call actions select the configured OpenClaw or installed Hermes integration.

steps.title: Return to standby
steps.detail: Expiry or stand-down invalidates the lease and resets active takeover state.

controlSummary: BRA starts with engagement-local paths and tool-specific operation checks. Registered SDK hooks add activity, target, token, and operator decisions. Capture and record gates then connect accepted findings to supporting material.

controlLayers.title: Engagement-local process state
controlLayers.mechanism: The wrapper places HOME, Claude state, temporary files, and XDG directories under body/.bra.
controlLayers.prevents: Routine SDK state is directed into the engagement workspace.
controlLayers.activation: Applied when run_agent builds the SDK options. Process identity and host permissions remain those of the launching user.
controlLayers.decision: Create engagement-local state directories and supply them to the SDK process.

controlLayers.title: Resolved file-operation paths
controlLayers.boundary: SDK Read, Grep, Glob, Write, and Edit requests
controlLayers.mechanism: The file adapter calls the Body guard. The guard resolves file paths before applying tool-specific policy.
controlLayers.prevents: Write/Edit requests cannot change layer1 through this path. State writes must match the declared locations.
controlLayers.activation: Registered in normal and documentation hooks. Missing, invalid, nonzero, or timed-out guard responses block. Reads have selected privacy restrictions.
controlLayers.attempt: Write body/layer1/rules/scope.md through the SDK Write tool.
controlLayers.decision: Return LAYER1_IMMUTABLE. A template-write or framework-development token does not override this rule.

controlLayers.title: Recognized Bash path references
controlLayers.boundary: Path tokens and write patterns in a Bash command string
controlLayers.mechanism: The approval hook resolves selected absolute path candidates. The Body guard checks recognized write contexts and restricted path substrings.
controlLayers.prevents: Non-exempt commands with detected outside paths are refused before ordinary invocation approval. Recognized restricted output paths are refused by Body policy.
controlLayers.activation: Approval path screening requires tool approval enabled and occurs after exemptions and session matches. Body checks require bash-guard.py to run.
controlLayers.attempt: Submit an unapproved Bash command that writes to /tmp/result.txt.
controlLayers.decision: The outside-path screen blocks first. It does not grant a tool approval for that detected path.

controlLayers.title: Local alias execution and return
controlLayers.boundary: Mapped Bash command execution inside the Body guard
controlLayers.mechanism: After original-command policy checks, the guard substitutes known aliases, runs a local shell, masks output, and returns a block-style preview.
controlLayers.prevents: The original SDK invocation is blocked after local execution, which avoids a second execution through that invocation.
controlLayers.activation: Requires readable mappings, a matching alias, and no ANON-DISABLE token. No second target check evaluates the substituted command.
controlLayers.attempt: Submit curl http://blanket/ with a known blanket mapping and matching tool permission.
controlLayers.decision: Execute the substituted local command, save masked output when available, and return ANON_INTERCEPT_OK with its actual exit code.

controlLayers.title: Recognized activity classes
controlLayers.boundary: Network and static patterns in the original Bash command
controlLayers.mechanism: The guard recognizes configured static, localhost, and network patterns. Network matches use YES, NO, or ASK activity state.
controlLayers.prevents: A recognized network test is refused when activity is NO, or ASK has no active-testing approval.
controlLayers.activation: Missing activity state becomes ASK. Static matches and localhost patterns bypass this activity gate. Other command checks still run.
controlLayers.attempt: Run nmap -sn 203.0.113.20 with activity ASK and no active-testing token.
controlLayers.decision: Return a block before target evaluation or execution.

controlLayers.title: Extracted target and scope level
controlLayers.boundary: One recognized target from the original Bash command
controlLayers.mechanism: The guard extracts a CIDR, IPv4 address, or recognized domain. Approval comes from original targets, discovered records, or literal scope text.
controlLayers.prevents: An extracted target absent from all accepted sources returns SCOPE_CHECK_REQUIRED. A resolved NONE level refuses interaction.
controlLayers.activation: Simple local commands bypass target extraction. Empty extraction skips this gate. Scope text and original targets resolve FULL before discovered levels. CUSTOM returns allow.
controlLayers.attempt: Run nmap -sn 203.0.113.20 with activity YES and no matching scope or target record.
controlLayers.decision: Refuse execution and request an operator scope decision. Word-only aliases have no post-substitution scope check.

controlLayers.title: Matched operation and scan tokens
controlLayers.boundary: Recognized dangerous, installation, push, and scan patterns
controlLayers.mechanism: The Body guard compares command patterns with environment or approval-file tokens. Aggressive scans accept a scan-class file or active-testing token.
controlLayers.prevents: A matching destructive, system-install, push, or aggressive-scan pattern can be refused without its applicable approval.
controlLayers.activation: Pattern-based checks apply when the Bash guard runs. Virtual-environment and user-install matches take earlier allow branches in the installation check.
controlLayers.attempt: Request a matched forced Git push without the required token.
controlLayers.decision: Return the first matched operation-token requirement. Separate policy checks continue only after that requirement passes.

controlLayers.title: Matching invocation and script authority
controlLayers.boundary: Non-exempt SDK tool requests and recognized script invocations
controlLayers.mechanism: The approval hook matches invocation files, retry identity, expiring retry grants, or session permission. Bash then checks recognized script paths.
controlLayers.prevents: An unapproved non-exempt request returns TOOL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED. A recognized script path without approval returns SCRIPT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED.
controlLayers.activation: Tool approval is enabled by default. Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, TaskOutput, and ToolSearch are exempt. Simple allowlisted Bash and internal layer1 paths are exempt.
controlLayers.attempt: Request nmap -sn 203.0.113.20 without any matching tool approval.
controlLayers.decision: Block for operator review. A granted tool approval does not add the target to scope.

controlLayers.title: Stop state before managed tool work
controlLayers.boundary: Registered pre-tool events and the Body Bash guard
controlLayers.mechanism: The SDK hook checks BRA_STOP, .bra/STOP, and the CLAUDE.md status block. The Body command guard checks stop state again.
controlLayers.prevents: An active stop returns a tool block. The command guard returns exit 99 before its command execution path.
controlLayers.activation: Stop is clear when none of the recognized signals is active. Hook decisions do not constitute host-wide process interception.
controlLayers.attempt: Create .bra/STOP before a managed Bash request.
controlLayers.decision: Return the stop decision. No approval token overrides the stop predicate.

controlLayers.title: Pending finding and documentation work
controlLayers.boundary: SDK tool selection while findings need documentation
controlLayers.mechanism: The normal finding hook restricts consequential work when the pending queue exists. Findings handoff also checks explicit file paths.
controlLayers.prevents: Normal queued finding work blocks non-read tools except selected finding writes. Handoff permits only its declared file tools and destinations.
controlLayers.activation: Read, Glob, and Grep remain allowed. Missing or unreadable queues allow. The documentation hook set omits finding guard; an active documentation subagent also releases it.
controlLayers.attempt: Request ordinary assessment work while a readable pending finding remains and no subagent flag is active.
controlLayers.decision: Return the documentation block. Later hooks can still run; alias execution has no separate finding-queue predicate.

controlLayers.title: Model-visible policy and task context
controlLayers.boundary: Prompts, method context, and compaction instructions
controlLayers.mechanism: The first normal turn includes CLAUDE.md. Method and phase routines supply the task context. Compaction restores governance text.
controlLayers.prevents: Guidance directs target selection, exclusions, methods, evidence use, and response to blocks. It does not itself refuse a host operation.
controlLayers.activation: Applied through normal prompt construction and PreCompact. A custom documentation system prompt uses a separate hook set and task contract.
controlLayers.attempt: Ask the agent to contact a target listed only as excluded scope prose.
controlLayers.decision: The model receives the exclusion instruction. Bash literal scope matching does not distinguish that exclusion section.

controlLayers.title: Captured output and source identity
controlLayers.boundary: Tool results and locally intercepted Bash output
controlLayers.mechanism: PostToolUse captures nonempty results, tool metadata, and artifact hashes. The alias intercept writes its own masked capture and provenance.
controlLayers.prevents: Source records make later attribution and local content checks possible. Capture does not authorize the completed operation.
controlLayers.activation: Post hooks and capture writes are best effort. Generic post capture masks saved artifacts when mappings load; it does not replace the SDK response.
controlLayers.attempt: A permitted tool returns nonempty output.
controlLayers.decision: Attempt to save a raw artifact and index its source. WATCH and TRACK add token-selected logs.

controlLayers.title: Finding acceptance and queue release
controlLayers.boundary: Structured finding record and referenced proof material
controlLayers.mechanism: The enforcer checks sections, metadata, placeholders, hash syntax, applicable local artifact content, and proof references or inline commands.
controlLayers.prevents: An incomplete or mismatched record remains pending. A marker alone cannot pass these record checks.
controlLayers.activation: Applies through validate_finding_record and queue reconciliation. N/A hashes are supported. Artifact checks apply to qualifying local references.
controlLayers.attempt: Complete a finding with a SHA-256 value that differs from its referenced local artifact.
controlLayers.decision: Return an invalid validation result and retain the pending finding. The check does not establish semantic exploit validity.

controlLayers.title: Scope, exceptions, and publication decisions
controlLayers.boundary: Managed approval interface and engagement records
controlLayers.mechanism: The manager records approval or denial, grants matching state, and selects continuation. Scope registration updates persistent target records.
controlLayers.prevents: A denial returns to operator choices without retrying that command. An unavailable grant does not create matching permission.
controlLayers.activation: Normal UI startup creates override history. Direct scope registration is a trusted backend helper; CLI registration consumes SCOPE-GRANT. Publication remains an operator review responsibility.
controlLayers.attempt: Deny a scope decision after SCOPE_CHECK_REQUIRED.
controlLayers.decision: Record the denial when history is active and return to awaiting input. No target grant is written.

controlLayers.title: Reviewed knowledge transfer
controlLayers.boundary: Checked pitch items and reusable template destinations
controlLayers.mechanism: Promotion selects checked, unimplemented items, routes recognized sections, and uses a temporary template-write token around supported destinations.
controlLayers.prevents: Unchecked proposals do not enter this promotion path. Reusable override advice does not become an active engagement exception.
controlLayers.activation: Approval is represented by checked pitch content. The trusted routine creates its own temporary token and removes it if created there. Existing tokens remain.
controlLayers.attempt: Promote a pitch containing one unchecked proposal and one checked tool entry.
controlLayers.decision: Skip the unchecked proposal. Route the accepted tool entry, mark it implemented, and record promotion activity.
